Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Apex Medical Devices Inc. Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Michael Chen, CFO; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Ramirez, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Medical Devices delivered strong results this quarter, driven by increasing adoption of our innovative medical devices and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover five key aspects of our performance:
1. Organic revenue growth by segment and geography
2. Hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates
3. FDA approvals and CE marks obtained
4. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
5. Revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year

Michael will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with organic revenue growth by segment and geography. This metric really highlights the strength of our core Medical Devices portfolio and our disciplined execution in a dynamic market. Just to remind everyone, organic growth excludes the effects of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange fluctuations. For the full year to date in 2024, we've achieved 8.7% organic revenue growth globally, picking up speed from 7.2% last year, thanks to solid procedural volume recovery, market share gains in fast-growing areas like structural heart and neuromodulation, and some average selling price uplift from our premium product mix.

Let me break it out by segment. Our business rests on four main franchises: Cardiovascular Solutions, Orthopedics & Spine, Diabetes & Patient Monitoring, and MedSurg Essentials. Focusing first on Q3 results and then the year trends.

Cardiovascular Solutions, which is 42% of our total revenue, grew organically by 12.4% in Q3 and 11.8% for the year so far. This was our top performer, powered by double-digit procedural increases in electrophysiology, structural heart, and cardiac rhythm management. In electrophysiology, our next-generation Watchtower™ mapping system, building on advancements like Biosense Webster's CARTO ecosystem, grabbed 2 points of share in the U.S. TAVR-adjacent EP market, with Q3 volumes up 18% year-over-year as ablation procedures caught up after COVID-related elective backlogs. Structural heart jumped 15%, led by our EvoGuard™ transcatheter mitral valve repair device, which experienced 25% U.S. adoption growth following positive CMS reimbursement changes, similar to the momentum around Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien platform. Cardiac rhythm management held steady at 9% organic growth, with our Micra VR2™ leadless pacemaker now making up over 40% of our implant mix, helping counter a short-term supply issue at a competitor like Abbott's Aveir platform. Margins in this segment improved by 120 basis points due to scale from our manufacturing expansion in Galway, Ireland.

Orthopedics & Spine, accounting for 28% of revenue, saw 7.2% organic growth in Q3 and 6.9% year-to-date, in line with peers like Stryker and Zimmer Biomet as hip and knee replacement volumes moderated. A key driver was our Triad™ robotic-assisted system, much like Stryker's Mako, which grew 22% in U.S. installs and lifted our knee procedure share by 1.5 points to 14%. Spine fusion advanced 10% thanks to our Vertex™ expandable interbody devices, aided by the shift to outpatient settings and ASC penetration, now at 35% of cases compared to 25% last year. We faced some ASP pressure in trauma from group purchasing organization consolidation, but countered it with 4% volume increases through surgeon education programs.

Diabetes & Patient Monitoring, 18% of our mix, sped up to 9.1% organic growth in Q3 and 8.5% for the year, surpassing Dexcom and Abbott's FreeStyle Libre in integrated CGM-insulin pump systems. Our LibreSync™ ecosystem reached 1.2 million active U.S. users, up 28%, with sensor ASP rising 3% on features like predictive hypo alerts. Patient monitoring grew 11% on our VitalLink™ remote telemetry beds, tapping into hospital capacity builds after the pandemic.

Lastly, MedSurg Essentials, 12% of revenue, posted reliable 5.3% Q3 and 4.8% year-to-date organic growth. Endoscopy tools such as our ScopeGuard™ single-use duodenoscopes increased 14% due to infection control requirements, echoing trends at Pentax Medical, while vascular access catheters dealt with 2% ASP decline from Vizient contracts but maintained steady volumes.

On geography, our U.S. business—65% of revenue—led with 9.2% organic growth year-to-date, improving from 7.8% in 2023, propelled by 11% procedural uptick in Medicare Advantage electives and $250 million in new GPO agreements with IDNs. EMEA, 20% of revenue, grew 7.1% organically, held back some by German DRG cuts but lifted by 15% UK structural heart uptake after NICE approvals for EvoGuard™. APAC, 12%, rocketed 12.8%, with China up 18% on our CRM portfolio amid the Healthy China 2030 initiative—adding over 500 new hospital listings—and Japan EP volumes up 20% through our J-MITRA partnership. Latin America, 3%, managed 6.4% despite Brazil forex swings, driven by orthopedics in private-pay markets.

These outcomes stem from our 'Innovate, Penetrate, Expand' strategy. We put $1.2 billion into R&D—14% of sales—enabling 25+ new product launches, like AI-driven procedural planning in Triad™ robotics, which boosted OR efficiency by 22% in beta sites. We gained 1.2 share points across franchises according to IQVIA, against flat 6.5% industry growth. Supply chain issues in semiconductors for CGMs were contained via dual-sourcing from TSMC and U.S. fabs, capping impact at 50 basis points. Ahead, we anticipate tailwinds from aging demographics—global over-65 population up 3% year-over-year—obesity-related T2D procedures, and U.S. IRA rules supporting domestic medtech production.

Now, let's talk about hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates. These continue to fuel our growth, especially in orthopedic navigation systems, robotic-assisted spine solutions, and our Vizor AI-Enabled Endoscopy platform. The shift from inpatient hospitals to cost-effective ASCs is speeding up, driven by CMS expanding the ASC-covered procedures list to 548 as of Q2 this year, covering high-volume orthopedics like total hip and knee replacements that make up over 30% of our U.S. procedure mix.

For Q3, overall adoption—measured as the percentage of eligible sites using our capital equipment or disposables at least quarterly—hit 32% across our U.S. addressable market of about 5,800 hospitals and 6,200 ASCs. That's up 8 points year-over-year and 3 sequentially from Q2. By venue:

Hospital adoption was 28%, up 4 points annually but flat quarter-over-quarter. We're gaining steadily in big IDNs like HCA Healthcare and Tenet, where Vizor OR efficiency gains—cutting procedure times by 22% per case based on real-world evidence—spur repeat placements. Hospitals trail due to 9-12 month sales cycles amid capital scrutiny and Medicare Advantage bundled payments, now covering 52% of beneficiaries. Our spine robotics attach rate in hospitals reached 65% in Q3, matching Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci benchmarks in soft tissue, following FDA 510(k) clearance for the FlexSpine 2.0 module with haptic feedback.

ASC adoption shone at 42%, up 18 points YoY and 6 sequentially. This tracks ASC procedure volumes growing 12% annually through 2027 per IDC Health Insights, 4x faster than hospitals. We're strong in Florida and Texas clusters, where operators like SCA Health and United Surgical Partners International standardize on us. Disposables use in ASCs averaged 18 kits per system monthly versus 12 in hospitals, yielding 35% higher ASP at $2,800 per ortho navigation kit. For instance, with Regent Surgical Health, we've hit 75% adoption across their 25 centers, enabling 85% same-day discharge for TKA procedures.

By region, U.S. leads at 35% overall, helped by No Surprises Act reimbursement stability and 15% sales force growth targeting ASCs. Europe is at 22%, up 7 points, via UK NICE guidelines for minimally invasive tech and CE Mark for Vizor AI, integrating with Siemens Healthineers imaging. Germany and Benelux drive 60% of EU hospital wins, though ASCs are early at 15% pending HTA. Asia-Pacific is 12% but growing 25% YoY in Japan after PMDA clearance, with Olympus endoscopy markets opening to Vizor—Terumo pilots showed 40% procedure time cuts.

Supporting trends include ASCs taking 55% of musculoskeletal procedures in 2024 per Definitive Healthcare, up from 42% in 2021; our systems fit with modular carts and wireless setup under 5 minutes. Value-based results like 28% readmission drops for Vizor endoscopies match UnitedHealthcare ORYX metrics. Our cloud-based Vizor Analytics dashboard, launched in May, aids MIPS reporting with 60% new-site adoption, pushing recurring revenue to 68%.

We're investing $150 million in ASC R&D, including a sub-$1M robotic arm for IDE in Q1 2025. Our ASC sales team grew 40% YoY, with 50-center PROPENSITY trials vs. Stryker Mako and Zimmer ROSA. We see hospital adoption stabilizing at 30-32% year-end, ASCs to 50%, contributing 25% of 2025 revenue, up from 18%.

Moving on to FDA approvals and CE marks obtained. Before we get deeper into financials, I want to spotlight our recent regulatory wins under FDA and EU MDR—these are critical for ramping revenue in cardiovascular interventions, neuromodulation, and structural heart. In Q3, we earned three FDA 510(k) clearances and one PMA, totaling nine U.S. approvals this year—80% more than 2022's five. The standout is PMA for our V-Core™ next-gen bioresorbable vascular scaffold for peripheral artery disease, using degradable magnesium struts and sirolimus polymer with 98% resorption in 12 months from our IDE trial. It follows our coronary scaffold's 12% share in the $4.2B U.S. DES market, competing with Abbott's XIENCE.

Trial data showed 92% target lesion revascularization-free at 24 months vs. 85% for nitinol stents like Boston Scientific's Eluvia. We price V-Core 15% premium, aiming $250M peak U.S. sales by 2026, launching to $45M FY24 in 150 cath labs. Also, 510(k)s for NeuroPulse™ RF ablation catheter with AI lesion mapping (95% first-pass isolation) and EchoGuide™ IVUS with 3D OCT, targeting 8-10% share in $1.8B EP ablation.

In Europe, CE marks from TÜV SÜD for those plus De Novo for HeartBridge™ transcatheter mitral valve repair—96% technical success, 2.1% 30-day mortality in 250-patient study, better than Medtronic Tendyne early results. MDR cost us $28M in R&D for surveillance and biocompatibility.

These open U.S. Medicare PAD reimbursement up 12% YoY to $2.1B for 600K procedures, partnering 40 IDNs like Mayo. In EU, Germany's $900M DRG market favors V-Core; China NMPA filing Q1 2024 for $1.5B APAC PAD at 14% CAGR from diabetes.

Our 92% regulatory hit rate over 24 months, up from 75%, comes from $150M R&D (18% revenue) on digital twins and adaptive trials, cutting V-Core by 6 months. This de-risks 15 products, including neuromodulation Breakthroughs.

Financially, prior approvals drove 22% of Q3's 15% growth ($312M total new), new ones add $180M FY24 at 65% margins. Long-term, 20-25% CAGR vs. 7% industry, cross-selling 4,200 accounts.

Next, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains. I'm pleased with our approach here, delivering efficiency that supported adjusted operating margin expansion to 28.2%, up 210 basis points year-over-year. Amid inflation, CMS headwinds, and supply disruptions like those peers faced in 2022-2023, SG&A fell to 24.8% of revenue from 27.1% prior year and 25.6% Q2—a $68M sequential and $142M YTD savings—while core revenue grew 9% constant currency on electrophysiology and structural heart strength.

Breaking down levers, where sales forces, compliance, and reimbursement drive 60-65% of medtech SG&A.

Sales force optimization and digital shift: In cardiovascular and orthopedics (55% revenue), we boosted productivity 12% via "Precision Selling," with Salesforce Einstein AI cutting case time 18% using Epicor data. Consolidated 15 U.S. Midwest territories to Sunbelt growth areas (volumes +14%); VR demos for Watchman FLX LAAC saved 22% travel ($14M QoQ), holding 92% adoption. Piloting Philips informatics to digitize 30% U.S. sales by year-end, like Intuitive teleproctoring.

G&A via SAP S/4HANA rollout saved 15% in finance/HR; UiPath RPA cut invoice cycles to 4 days ($21M annualized). Procurement council with DuPont/3M cut indirect spend 11% ($32M YTD) on guidewires/catheter consumables amid 8-10% inflation. Reduced corporate headcount 4% (100 roles), upskilling sales; R&D intact at 1,200.

Regionally: U.S. (52% revenue) 190 bps leverage on rep ratios, Outcomes360 RWE boosting win rates 7% vs. Edwards Sapien. EMEA (32%) 9% cut via Dublin shared services/Veeva Vault, offsetting euro weakness. APAC (12%) $8M Japan compliance savings, higher China marketing vs. MicroPort. LATAM 13% procurement localization.

Our trailing SG&A at 25.2% beats peer 26.8%, nearing Boston Scientific's 23.5%. Savings fund M&A like $250M peptide platform. Expect 23.5-24.0% year-end ($200M savings), cushioning risks like IRA changes.

Finally, revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year. For Q4 2024, we guide total revenue $1.42B-$1.46B, 9-13% YoY or 10-14% organic, atop Q3's $1.38B (11% organic).

By segment: Cardiovascular (52%) 12-15% organic on Watchman FLX Pro (+250 bps U.S. share vs. Boston/Abbott), EMIA tempered by Japan pricing. Orthopedics/Spine (28%) 8-11% on ApexFlex robotics (+15% volumes), Brazil/India trauma. Neuromodulation/Diagnostics (20%) 7-10% on NeuroPulse DBS expanded labels, China VBP.

Regions: U.S. (65%) mid-teens on OR reps/IDNs; Europe (20%) 6-9% despite Germany DiGA, UK NICE wins; APAC/China (10%) double-digit on Suzhou plant, NRDL pricing; RoW (5%) high-teens LATAM.

Q4 margins: gross 68.5-69.5% (+120 bps) on alloy sourcing, robotics mix (75% vs. 60%); operating 24.5-25.5% (+150 bps) on $25M LeanMed savings; EPS $1.85-$1.95 (22% tax, 150M shares).

For FY2025, revenue $5.85B-$6.00B, 8-11% growth or 9-12% organic (+1% M&A like $450M endoscopy).

Segments: Cardiovascular 11-14% on ApexValve Ultra TAVR vs. Sapien; Ortho/Spine 9-12% AR/VR nav; Neuro 10-13% closed-loop SCS (+30% responders vs. Medtronic).

Regions: U.S. 12-15% IRA/CAPEX; Europe 7-10% MDR/EU4Health; China/APAC 14-17% JDCET; RoW 15-18% ASEAN.

FY25 margins: gross 69-70% (+200 bps) scale/R&D AI/scrap cuts/tantalum stabilization; operating 25.5-26.5% ($100M automation); EBITDA ~32%, FCF >95%; EPS $8.10-$8.40 (+2-3% buybacks).

This ties to 'Precision Growth 2025': 12 launches (PAD scaffold vs. BD Eluvia, ApexCloud RPM with Epic/Cerner); 200 bps share via ORBIT-AF RWE (25% lower readmits PFA vs. RF); inventory to 7.5 months, 30% recycled Ti; $1-1.5B M&A (ROIC >20%).

Risks: elective delays, MA cliffs, J&J competition, FX (40% EUR/JPY); 60% Q4 booked. Positions us for above-market growth in $550B medtech at 5-6% CAGR.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen for a review of our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena outlined comprehensively, we delivered a strong financial performance this quarter, with Q3 revenue of $1.38 billion reflecting 11% organic growth, robust margins at 67.3% gross and 28.2% adjusted operating, and continued leverage in SG&A. Expenses were well-controlled, profitability exceeded expectations with adjusted EPS ahead, and our balance sheet remains solid with ample liquidity for R&D and M&A. Full details are in our release, aligning with the guidance Elena shared.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj Patel for an update on our product pipeline.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Michael. I'm excited to share updates on our innovative pipeline. We recently received FDA clearance for V-Core™, our groundbreaking bioresorbable vascular scaffold that promises to revolutionize PAD treatment with full resorption and superior outcomes. Building on that, we're advancing NeuroPulse™ for AF ablation and HeartBridge™ for mitral repair, with clinical data showing best-in-class results. In robotics, Triad™ and FlexSpine 2.0 are ramping, and our AI Vizor platform is driving efficiency gains. We've got 15 products in the queue, including closed-loop neuromodulation and ApexValve Ultra TAVR, supported by $1.2 billion R&D. These position us for 20%+ CAGR in new revenue streams.

Now, back to Elena for Q&A.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Raj. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Elena or Michael, on the organic growth in cardiovascular—can you expand on the share gains in EP and structural heart, and any update on ASP dynamics?

Elena Vasquez:
Great question, John. In cardiovascular, our 12.4% Q3 organic growth came from EP's Watchtower™ capturing 2 share points with 18% volume surge, structural heart's EvoGuard™ at 15% on CMS tailwinds, and CRM's Micra VR2™ at 40% mix. ASPs held with premium mix, modest expansion offsetting any pressures—expect continuation into Q4 with 12-15% guide.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Hi team, solid adoption numbers. On ASCs surging to 42%, how sustainable is that versus hospitals, and any color on international ramp?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, Emily. ASC growth is durable at 12% annual volumes, our 42% penetration with 18 kits/month drives higher ASPs. Hospitals steady at 28% amid cycles, but attach rates like 65% spine robotics help. Internationally, Europe at 22% on Vizor CE, Japan 12% growing fast—aiming 50% ASC U.S. by next year, 25% revenue contribution.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Question on regulatory wins—how do V-Core and HeartBridge impact near-term revenue, and pipeline velocity?

Lisa Ramirez:
Hi David, from a commercial view, V-Core launches Q4 in 150 labs for $45M FY24 ramp, $250M peak at 15% premium on strong PAD data. HeartBridge unlocks EU structural heart post-MDR. Our 92% hit rate and cross-sell to 4,200 accounts add $180M FY24—velocity high with digital twins accelerating timelines.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for that insight, Lisa.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thanks. On SG&A leverage and guidance, any risks to the 23.5-24% target, and FY25 margin drivers?

Raj Patel:
Maria, SG&A efficiencies from AI CRM, RPA, procurement hold firm—$200M savings with peer-beating 25.2%. FY25 gross to 69-70% on scale, AI R&D, deflation; operating 25.5-26.5% automation. Risks like FX/IRA baked in, cushion from 65%+ gross margins.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
